options.name: --version
options.description: Output the jq version and exit with zero

options.name: --seq
options.description: Use the application/json-seq MIME type scheme for separating JSON texts in jq's input and output

options.name: --stream
options.description: Parse the input in streaming fashion, outputting arrays of path and leaf values

options.name: --slurp
options.description: Instead of running the filter for each JSON object in the input, read the entire input stream into a large array and run the filter just once

options.name: -s
options.description: Instead of running the filter for each JSON object in the input, read the entire input stream into a large array and run the filter just once

options.name: --raw-input
options.description: Don't parse the input as JSON. Instead, each line of text is passed to the filter as a string

options.name: -R
options.description: Don't parse the input as JSON. Instead, each line of text is passed to the filter as a string

options.name: --null-input
options.description: Don't read any input at all! Instead, the filter is run once using null as the input

options.name: -n
options.description: Don't read any input at all! Instead, the filter is run once using null as the input

options.name: --compact-output
options.description: By default, jq pretty-prints JSON output. Using this option will result in more compact output by instead putting each JSON object on a single line

options.name: -c
options.description: By default, jq pretty-prints JSON output. Using this option will result in more compact output by instead putting each JSON object on a single line

options.name: --tab
options.description: Use a tab for each indentation level instead of two spaces

options.name: --indent
options.description: Use the given number of spaces for indentation

options.name: --color-output
options.description: By default, jq outputs colored JSON if writing to a terminal. You can force it to produce color even if writing to a pipe or a file using -C

options.name: -C
options.description: By default, jq outputs colored JSON if writing to a terminal. You can force it to produce color even if writing to a pipe or a file using -C

options.name: --monochrome-output
options.description: Disable color

options.name: -M
options.description: Disable color

options.name: --ascii-output
options.description: Jq usually outputs non-ASCII Unicode codepoints as UTF-8, even if the input specified them as escape sequences

options.name: -a
options.description: Jq usually outputs non-ASCII Unicode codepoints as UTF-8, even if the input specified them as escape sequences

options.name: --unbuffered
options.description: Flush the output after each JSON object is printed

options.name: --sort-keys
options.description: Output the fields of each object with the keys in sorted orde

options.name: -S
options.description: Output the fields of each object with the keys in sorted orde

options.name: --raw-output
options.description: If the filter's result is a string then it will be written directly to standard output rather than being formatted as a JSON string with quotes

options.name: -r
options.description: If the filter's result is a string then it will be written directly to standard output rather than being formatted as a JSON string with quotes

options.name: --join-output
options.description: Like -r but jq won't print a newline after each output

options.name: -j
options.description: Like -r but jq won't print a newline after each output

options.name: -f
options.description: Read filter from the file rather than from a command line

options.name: --from-file
options.description: Read filter from the file rather than from a command line

options.name: -L
options.description: Prepend directory to the search list for modules

options.name: -e
options.description: Sets the exit status of jq to 0 if the last output values was neither false nor null, 1 if the last output value was either false or null, or 4 if no valid result was ever produced

options.name: --exit-status
options.description: Sets the exit status of jq to 0 if the last output values was neither false nor null, 1 if the last output value was either false or null, or 4 if no valid result was ever produced

options.name: --arg
options.description: This option passes a value to the jq program as a predefined variable

options.name: --argjson
options.description: This option passes a JSON-encoded value to the jq program as a predefined variable

options.name: --slurpfile
options.description: This option reads all the JSON texts in the named file and binds an array of the parsed JSON values to the given global variable

options.name: --rawfile
options.description: This option reads in the named file and binds its contents to the given global variable

options.name: --args
options.description: Remaining arguments are positional string arguments. These are available to the jq program as $ARGS.positional[]

options.name: --jsonargs
options.description: Remaining arguments are positional JSON text arguments. These are available to the jq program as $ARGS.positional[]

options.name: --run-tests
options.description: Runs the tests in the given file or standard input. This must be the last option given and does not honor all preceding options

args.name: filter
args.description: Must be enclosed in single quotes
